records.label: The drawing of the straws

refs.q: King of Upmeads
Hugh goeth north with Lancelot

records.summary: The brothers draw lots: longest goes north, next east, third west, shortest stays as King of Upmeads; Ralph draws the shortest.

records.label: Deaths in the Wood Debateable

refs.q: the Wood Debateable

records.summary: King Peter's father and eldest son were slain in battle in the forest.

records.label: The brothers' departure

refs.q: Nicholas

records.summary: The three elder brothers ride off from the Four-want-way; Nicholas leads Ralph's war-horse home.

records.label: King Peter lost in the Wood Debateable

refs.q: belated there all alone

records.summary: The king, belated alone in the forest, was treated kindly by outlaws.

records.label: Ralph's secret departure

refs.q: went his ways splashing across the ford, before the sun had arisen

records.summary: Ralph arms in the willow copse by the Ford and rides south before sunrise.

records.label: The gift of the necklace

refs.q: so that it shall be to thee as if thou hadst drunk of the WELL AT THE WORLD'S END

records.summary: Dame Katherine gives Ralph the necklace and tells of the Well at the World's End.

records.label: The Dry Tree has been seen

refs.q: I have spoken to one who hath heard of him who hath seen it

records.summary: Clement has spoken to one who heard of a man who saw the Dry Tree but did not drink of the Well.

records.label: First meeting with the man of the leafless tree

refs.q: The first time!

records.summary: At Netherton churchyard the green rider shoves past Ralph and cries "The first time!"

records.label: Ralph's oath to the shepherds

refs.q: Thou hast sworn an oath, and it is a good oath

records.summary: Ralph drinks with the shepherds and swears to be a good lord to them; they give him the beacon and watchword.

records.label: Past sightings of the green rider

refs.q: In my lifetime such a man hath, to my knowledge, been seen thrice before

records.summary: The rider has been seen thrice before in the old shepherd's lifetime, each before evil days.

records.label: Second meeting with the man of the leafless tree

refs.q: The second time!

records.summary: In the kneeling crowd a hidden-faced man-at-arms whispers "The second time!"

records.label: St. John's Eve at Higham
participants: Abbot of St. Mary's of Higham

refs.q: this was St. John's Eve

records.summary: Plays, bale-fire, procession of the Abbot.

records.label: Ralph's dream

refs.q: the water itself was gone, and he was casting his angle on to a dry road

records.summary: Ralph dreams of fishing in Upmeads Water until the water is gone and he casts on a dry road.

records.label: The monk's offer of the chaplet

refs.q: he was determined not to chaffer away his gossip's gift for any shaveling's token

records.summary: The monk tries to have Ralph leave Dame Katherine's necklace with him in exchange for a blessed chaplet; Ralph refuses.

records.label: The maiden of Bourton Abbas

refs.q: kissed her many times

records.summary: Ralph meets the grieving maiden, who warns him of the Wood and kisses him farewell.

records.label: Loss of the maiden's lover

refs.q: his horse has come back, and the reins and the saddle all bloody

records.summary: Her lover rode alone into the Wood Perilous five days ago; his horse returned bloody.

records.label: Capture at the crossroads

refs.q: Oliver!  Oliver! lead on the way thou wottest!

records.summary: Ralph is seized by the Burg's company, questioned, recognised by Oliver, and left behind when a runner arrives.

records.label: Rescue of the lady at the crossroads

refs.q: Smite him, smite!  O lovely creature of God!

records.summary: Ralph kills two men leading a captive lady; she warns him off the Burg, kisses him and rides south-east.
records.time_text: sunset, about five hours after noon onward

records.label: The maiden's departure for the Well

refs.q: rode away east toward Hampton

records.summary: The maiden of Bourton refuses Ralph's company and rides east to seek the Well.

records.label: Chase by the Dry Tree riders

refs.q: Ha, thieves!  I am Roger of the Rope-walk

records.summary: Four Dry Tree horsemen chase Ralph and Roger; arrows miss; they reach the highway and the pursuers turn back.

records.label: Founding of the Burg

refs.q: the Fair Lady who erewhile began the building of the Burg

records.summary: The Fair Lady began the Burg when wedded to the Forest Lord.

records.label: Entry into the Burg

refs.q: Ralph Motherson

records.summary: Ralph enters by the North Gate as "Ralph Motherson"; Roger is appointed his man.

records.label: Failed escape of the Queen

refs.q: it is to be feared that she hath slipped through our fingers once more

records.summary: The Burg hoped to take the Dry Tree's witch but she has slipped away.

records.label: Return of the Burg's host

refs.q: to see the host mustered and the spoil blessed

records.summary: The host returns through the South Gate with spoil and women captives; it is mustered and the spoil blessed in the Great Place.

records.label: Third sighting of the man of the leafless tree
participants: (unnamed) small cloaked man at the Flower de Luce

refs.q: he deemed that he was the very man whom he had seen last in the Great Place at Higham

records.summary: The big man in a sallet and white gaberdine leaves the Flower de Luce with a small cloaked companion.

records.label: Wheat-wearer conquest and Yule uprising

refs.q: rose up against them as occasion served, in the winter season and the Yule feast

records.summary: Wheat-wearers took the Burg and ruled three generations; the grandsons rose at Yule and slew them.

records.label: Roger's oath of service

refs.q: if thou goest I will go with thee

records.summary: Roger swears to follow Ralph wherever he goes.

records.label: Escape from the Burg

refs.q: The third time!

records.summary: Roger and Dry Tree men take Ralph out by a postern before dawn; Falcon is lost; the big man cries "The third time!"

records.label: Rescue of the Dry Tree prisoners

refs.q: here be all we four well met again

records.summary: The four captured woodmen are freed and rejoin their company in the wood.

records.label: Ralph accepts Roger's guidance

refs.q: I will ride with thee first to that fair house

records.summary: Ralph agrees to follow Roger to his master's house in hope of seeing the lady.

records.label: Arrival at the House of Abundance
participants: (unnamed) carline of the House of Abundance

refs.q: Now we are come home

records.summary: After a night ride Ralph and Roger reach the white castle at dawn and are served by an old woman.

records.label: Waiting at the Castle of Abundance
participants: (unnamed) carline of the House of Abundance

refs.q: there he slew a hart with one shaft

records.summary: Ralph waits the two days Roger asked, explores the castle and land, and hunts a hart.

records.label: The Lady's coming to Abundance

refs.q: but that was before the coming of the Lady of Abundance

records.summary: Peace came to the land with the Lady of Abundance, before the old man's birth.

records.label: Tale of the woman of the book

refs.q: whereof befel long and grievous war which she abode not to the end

records.summary: Wildwood maiden wed by a king's son, war over her, thraldom to a sorceress, rescue by a Well-seeker, escape from robbers, drinking of the Well.

records.label: Meeting the Vicar

refs.q: therewith suddenly he fell a-weeping

records.summary: Ralph meets the Vicar in the wood and walks back with him; the Vicar praises the Lady and weeps.

records.label: Ralph's three days of waiting
participants: (unnamed) carline of the House of Abundance

refs.q: thrice have I been away long from the castle and all has gone well

records.summary: Ralph wavers between searching the wood and waiting at the castle.

records.label: Fight by the lake

refs.q: I will give thee my body for his life

records.summary: The Knight of the Sun strikes down Walter the Black, then beats Ralph; the lady saves Ralph and bargains herself for his life.

records.label: Walter found alive

refs.q: this my friend Walter the Black is alive still

records.summary: The Knight of the Sun weeps over Walter and finds him alive; the lady dresses his wound.

records.label: The friar's coming

refs.q: lo, it was a holy man, a hermit in the habit of the Blackfriars

records.summary: A hermit rows down the lake at sunset, sent (he says) by speaking thornbushes, and takes charge of Walter.

records.label: The Lady takes Ralph from the lake

refs.q: now I have brought thee away from death

records.summary: Before dawn the Lady leads Ralph away from the Knight of the Sun; in a stone-ring clearing she reveals her marriage and they become lovers.

records.label: The Lady's expulsion from Sunway

refs.q: driven forth wrung with anguish, barefoot and bleeding

records.summary: On Walter's tale the Knight of the Sun cursed and drove out his bride before they were bedded.

records.label: Rest by the brook

refs.q: fell to speaking to him, as a tale is told in the ingle nook

records.summary: The lovers rest and eat at a brook before the Lady tells her story.

records.label: The self-weaving loom

refs.q: At last one day of late summer when I, now of some fifteen summers

records.summary: At fifteen, in a storm, the girl sees a loom weaving alone and the woman singing naked from a book.
records.time_text: late summer, the Lady about fifteen

records.label: Sacrifice of the white goat

refs.q: cut the beast's throat

records.summary: The witch sacrifices the girl's goat on the yew-ring altar.

records.label: The dead seeker in the snow

refs.q: dug a pit, and buried the poor damsel there with all her gear

records.summary: The girl finds a dead woman seeker; the witch takes her necklace; the girl buries her.

records.label: Four seekers visit the witch

refs.q: there came from the wood four men, a-horseback and weaponed

records.summary: Four armed riders come seeking a guide to the Well; the witch meets them in poor homespun.

records.label: Meeting the wise carline

refs.q: fell to teaching me wisdom

records.summary: In May the girl meets the wise old woman in the Dale of Lore and is taught there daily.

records.label: The king's son on Midsummer Day
participants: (unnamed) king's son of the Lady's youth
places: (unnamed) waste plain above the Dale of Lore

refs.q: I am as one whom the Avenger of Blood followeth

records.summary: A Well-seeking king's son meets the girl, loves her, gives her his necklace and rides on.

records.label: Death of the witch

refs.q: she fell across my feet

records.summary: The witch attacks the girl, who kills her with the carline's knife.

records.label: Return of the king's son
participants: (unnamed) king's son of the Lady's youth

refs.q: O my beloved, I have found thee, but I am faint with hunger

records.summary: Starving and defeated, the king's son returns to the Dale of Lore; the girl agrees to go with him.

records.label: Journey west out of the wilderness
participants: (unnamed) king's son of the Lady's youth
places: (unnamed) heathen simple folk beyond the mountains

refs.q: After we had passed long deserts of wood and heath, and gone through lands exceeding evil and perilous

records.summary: The Lady and the king's son cross the wilderness, stony waste and mountains to the heathen folk.

records.label: Welcome by the king
participants: (unnamed) king, father of the king's son
(unnamed) king, father of the king's son
(unnamed) king's son of the Lady's youth

refs.q: 'Yea,' said my lord, and therewith lifted my hand to his lips and kissed it

records.summary: The king meets his son outside the chief city; the son says he found the Well and kisses the Lady's hand.

records.label: Trial and rescue of the Lady
participants: (unnamed) king's son of the Lady's youth
(unnamed) king, father of the king's son
(unnamed) king, father of the king's son
places: (unnamed) Great Square of the Tower city

refs.q: Life for our Lord's Lady!

records.summary: Condemned for sorcery, the Lady is rescued at the stake by the prince's friends; the Bishop stops the fighting; truce and exile.

records.label: War of the Tower

refs.q: abode a long while, some two years, in the wilderness, living like outlaws and wolves' heads

records.summary: Years of war between the king and his son; the Lady loses two sons; two years as outlaws with the Dry Tree.

records.label: Dry Tree battle at Bear Castle

refs.q: fought a battle there with the Captain of Higham

records.summary: The Dry Tree rode over the Downs to Bear Castle and fought the Captain of Higham.

records.label: Triumph and reign
participants: (unnamed) king's son of the Lady's youth

refs.q: I sat a crowned Queen upon the throne

records.summary: After the old king's death the Lady and her lord enter the master city and she is enthroned where she was to be burned.

records.label: Return of the Teacher of Lore

refs.q: 'tis a score of years since we two sat in the Dale

records.summary: About twenty years after the Dale, the Teacher comes young again and invites the Lady to seek the Well.

records.label: Flight from the Tower

refs.q: So I vanished away from my throne and my kingdom

records.summary: After her lord's death the Lady leaves her throne disguised, in April, with the Teacher.

records.label: The Lady drinks of the Well

refs.q: Shortly to say it, we found the Well, and drank of its waters

records.summary: The Lady and the Teacher find the Well and drink.

records.label: The Teacher departs

refs.q: At last, and that was but some five years ago

records.summary: About five years ago the Teacher leaves for the most ancient parts of the world.

records.label: Geoffrey finds the Lady

refs.q: Geoffrey, what became of the white hind after the banners had left the wildwood

records.summary: Geoffrey and his sons reach the House of the Sorceress; she proves herself by old memories.
records.time_text: a month after the Teacher left

records.label: The maiden of Bourton freed

refs.q: went with her into the wildwood, and taught her wisdom of the way

records.summary: The Lady frees the maiden from the Dry Tree's prison and sends her toward the Well with the dead seeker's chaplet.
records.time_text: night after Ralph left the Burg

records.label: Death of the Lady of Abundance

refs.q: The witch is dead, the whore is dead!

records.summary: The Knight of the Sun finds the Lady at the cave and kills her; Ralph shoots him dead.

records.label: Burials in the desert

refs.q: He took up the body of the Lady

records.summary: Ralph entombs the Lady in the cave under stones and raises a cairn over the Knight.

records.label: Ralph leaves the wilderness
places: (unnamed) sheep downs by the Swelling Flood

refs.q: in short it was another world from the desert

records.summary: Grieving, Ralph walks out of the desert to the peopled Swelling Flood valley.

records.label: Ralph meets Blaise
places: (unnamed) highway ford of the Swelling Flood

refs.q: O happy day! when two of the Upmeads kindred meet thus in an alien land!

records.summary: At the hill above the ford Ralph meets Blaise and Richard and rides with them to Whitwall.

records.label: The Swevenham seekers depart

refs.q: I mind me the setting forth of these three

records.summary: Fifty years ago three Swevenham youths set out for the Well with music and flowers.

records.label: Ralph meets Clement in Whitwall

refs.q: it is the kiss of the gossip which she bade me give thee

records.summary: Clement brings Dame Katherine's kiss and news of Upmeads, and offers Ralph his company east.

records.label: The dream at Whitwall

refs.q: I hight Dorothea

records.summary: Ralph dreams of the Lady's farewell and of the maiden naming herself Dorothea.

records.label: Chaplet-wearing women on the east highway

refs.q: he came on one riding the highway, just about where the other woman had been seen

records.summary: Twice a lone woman with a gem chaplet, armed, is met on the highway thirty miles east of Whitwall, bound for the Well.

records.label: Twenty years ago: the great sickness

refs.q: five of our young men, calling to mind all the tales concerning the Well at the World's End, went their ways to seek it

records.summary: Five Swevenham youths swear to bring back Well-water and never return.

records.label: Richard's farewell counsel

refs.q: I will now tell thee the tale of my grief

records.summary: Richard hears Ralph's tale and counsels him before the company leaves.

records.label: Departure from Whitwall

refs.q: This is also a farewell to the House where I was born and bred

records.summary: Ralph leaves Whitwall with Clement's armed merchant company.

records.label: News of the captive maiden

refs.q: he was bound to seek her, and deliver her from thralldom

records.summary: At the Mid-Mountain House Ralph learns a woman like the maiden of Bourton was taken captive and sent to market.

records.label: Battle in the mountains

refs.q: Ralph ran in under the stroke and caught him by the throat and drew him out of the press

records.summary: The merchant company breaks through the strong-thieves' ambush; Ralph captures Bull Shockhead.

records.label: Ralph learns of the captor

refs.q: But, lord, I will do my best to find her for thee

records.summary: Bull tells Ralph his kinsman Bull Nosy took the maiden to Cheaping Knowe.

records.label: Arrival at Cheaping Knowe

refs.q: so came to the hostel of the Merchants, called the Fleece

records.summary: The merchant company enters Cheaping Knowe with banners and lodges at the Fleece.

records.label: Visit to the thrall-merchant

refs.q: Sir, I believe surely that I have seen this damsel

records.summary: Ralph learns the damsel was refused sale and probably taken toward Whiteness and the Lord of Utterbol.

records.label: News at Whiteness

refs.q: the damsel and he alone, and she with her hands unbound and riding a little horse

records.summary: The Deacon says the wild man left Whiteness with the damsel toward the Goldburg pass.

records.label: Discovery of Bull Nosy's body

refs.q: It is a man of my kindred, even he that was leading away thy she-friend

records.summary: The company finds the damsel's captor dead in the mountains; Ralph searches for her in vain.

records.label: Vision of Dorothea

refs.q: a great chamber builded of marble and done about with gold and bright colours

records.summary: Ralph sees her in a vision, alive and lamenting in a marble and gold chamber.

records.label: Founding of Goldburg

refs.q: that lord was slain in a tumult

records.summary: A lord built Goldburg as his home for the long life he hoped the Well would give; he was slain in a tumult.

records.label: Arrival at Goldburg

refs.q: One by one they passed through the wicket of the gate

records.summary: The merchant company enters Goldburg through the bridge-gate.

records.label: Audience with the Queen of Goldburg
places: (unnamed) High House of the Queen of Goldburg

refs.q: O that I might be thy friend in such-wise!

records.summary: Ralph tells the Queen his story; she promises help and later gives him a letter and confesses her love.
records.time_text: fifth and eighth days in Goldburg

records.label: Morfinn offers to guide Ralph

refs.q: I can be a shower of the way and a leader to any worthy knight

records.summary: Morfinn shows Utterbol's let-pass and offers to lead Ralph through Utterness to a sage.

records.label: Ralph frees Bull

refs.q: this is the token whereby it shall be known amongst our folk that I have made thee my brother

records.summary: Ralph frees Bull Shockhead, who makes him his brother.

records.label: Morfinn's news of the captive

refs.q: As I left Utterbol a month ago, I saw a damsel brought in captive there

records.summary: Morfinn describes the damsel brought captive into Utterbol a month ago.

records.label: Ralph taken by the Lord of Utterbol

refs.q: he is a goodly and well-fashioned a young man as was ever sold

records.summary: Morfinn delivers Ralph to the Lord of Utterbol's camp; Ralph is appraised and held.

records.label: March toward Utterness

refs.q: why dost thou suffer me to lead thee along whither thou wouldest not?

records.summary: Ralph rides captive in the Lord's train and learns of Utterbol's policy and Goldburg's legends.

records.label: Ralph sings for the Lord of Utterbol

refs.q: knew this for the first hour of his thralldom

records.summary: Ordered to sing on pain of beating, Ralph sings two songs; the Lord plans to test him at arms.

records.label: The Lord meets his Lady at the Dale of the Tower

refs.q: I have cheapened a likely thrall of Morfinn the Unmanned, and he is a gift to thee

records.summary: The Lady of Utterbol comes to meet the Lord; he offers her Ralph as a gift; she is struck by him.

records.label: The Lady's confession to Agatha

refs.q: I may help thee somewhat therein

records.summary: The Lady of Utterbol confesses love for Ralph; Agatha agrees to plot for her.

records.label: The joust at the Dale of the Tower

refs.q: We have no might against this youngling, man to man

records.summary: Ralph defeats Utterbol's best in sharp-spear jousts and wins a boon.

records.label: Redhead's warning

refs.q: Go thou not to Utterbol whatever may betide

records.summary: Redhead warns Ralph against Utterbol and plans his escape.

records.label: Ralph declared free

refs.q: I can see the string which is tied to thy leg, though thou feelest it not

records.summary: The Lord sourly frees Ralph with his arms; Otter warns the freedom is illusory.

records.label: The false Queen revealed

refs.q: What then! this woman is not the Queen?

records.summary: Ralph sees the woman riding with the Lord and realises she is not the Queen.

records.label: Redhead keeps tryst

refs.q: I shall be behind it abiding thee

records.summary: Redhead arranges Ralph's night escape at the dead oak with a fresh horse.

records.label: Agatha's ruse

refs.q: it is I who have drawn thee hither from the camp

records.summary: Agatha lures Ralph with a staged rescue, then confesses and lets him go.

records.label: Ralph's escape from the Utterbol camp
places: (unnamed) doddered oak at the forest camp

refs.q: Redhead kneeled to him one moment of time and then arose and went off into the night

records.summary: Ralph flees the camp at night on Redhead's horse.

records.label: Ralph rides alone toward the mountains

refs.q: though the sight was terrible, yet it gladdened him, since he knew that he was on the right way

records.summary: Free, Ralph rides east through wood and hills toward the mountain wall.

records.label: Ralph and Ursula meet in the pine wood
places: (unnamed) great pine wood under the mountains

refs.q: O, but I have kissed thy face before!  O, my friend, my friend!

records.summary: In the dark wood Ralph meets Ursula, who has escaped Utterbol, and they agree to seek the Well together.

records.label: Death of Bull Nosy

refs.q: lifted up his hand twice, and let it fall twice

records.summary: The Lord of Utterbol meets Bull Nosy and Ursula in the Goldburg mountains; Bull refuses to sell her and is killed.

records.label: Ursula resists the Lord

refs.q: bade him beware lest I should slay him or myself

records.summary: On the road to Utterbol the Lord threatens Ursula; she threatens to kill him or herself; he backs down.

records.label: Meeting the Sage of Swevenham

refs.q: I am glad that ye are come at last; for I looked for you no later than this

records.summary: The Sage finds them at dawn and takes them to his house to teach them.

records.label: Lessons at the ancient altar

refs.q: till they were waxen wise in the matters of the Well at the World's End

records.summary: Over two days the Sage reads and drills Ralph and Ursula in the way to the Well.

records.label: The Sage's illusion
participants: (unnamed) nephew of the Lord of Utterbol

refs.q: O Otter, this is an evil place of an evil deed!

records.summary: The Sage hides the travellers from the Utterbol riders by an illusion of bones and stones.

records.label: The Sage's charge at the ridge

refs.q: they brought down Heaven to the Earth for a little while

records.summary: Facing the mountains, the Sage charges the lovers on how to live, and they state their aims.

records.label: Crossing the Sea of Molten Rocks

refs.q: the Sage led through it all unfumbling

records.summary: Over about four days the Sage leads them by the token route through the lava, past earth-fires.

records.label: The Candle of the Giants kindles

refs.q: it will be for a token to them there

records.summary: The fire on the Candle of the Giants is held to bode ill for the Lord of Utterbol.

records.label: Parting from the Sage at the Gate

refs.q: he drew himself away from them, and turned about with no word more, and went his ways

records.summary: The Sage brings them to the Fighting Man and leaves; they enter the pass.

records.label: Arrival in the Vale of Sweet Chestnuts

refs.q: they knew that they had come to their winter house

records.summary: After thirty days in the mountains they reach the wintering vale and its marked cavern.

records.label: Winter in the mountains

refs.q: So wore autumn into winter, and the frost came, and the snow

records.summary: Ralph and Ursula winter in the Vale of Sweet Chestnuts as friends.

records.label: Ursula and the bear

refs.q: he cast himself upon her without a word, and kissed her greedily

records.summary: Ralph kills a bear chasing Ursula; they declare their love and pledge to wed.

records.label: Wedding of Ralph and Ursula

refs.q: then those twain kissed the newcomers and departed to their bridal bower hand in hand

records.summary: Witnessed by the Innocent Folk's messengers, Ralph and Ursula wed by moonlight.

records.label: Welcome by the Innocent Folk

refs.q: Welcome and thrice welcome to the Seekers after length of days

records.summary: The Innocent Folk receive Ralph and Ursula in their Mote-house as "Seekers after length of days".

records.label: Arrival at the House of the Sorceress

refs.q: wept long for the friend whose feet had worn that path so often

records.summary: Ralph and Ursula reach the kept House where the Lady was a thrall; Ralph weeps.

records.label: Reading at the Sorceress's altar

refs.q: day after day betimes in the morning they bore the said book to the altar and read therein

records.summary: For eight days they read the House's lore-book at the ancient altar.

records.label: Crossing the Thirsty Desert

refs.q: Ralph and Ursula buried these two with the heaping of stones

records.summary: The lovers cross the salt ridges among the dried dead, burying some.

records.label: At the Dry Tree

refs.q: then from both their lips at once came the cry THE DRY TREE

records.summary: The lovers find the Dry Tree; Ursula prevents Ralph drinking the poisoned pool and lures him away.

records.label: Out of the Thirsty Desert

refs.q: they drank their fill and watered their horses abundantly

records.summary: Nearly out of water, they reach a safe river and recover.

records.label: Arrival at the World's End

refs.q: it was no long time ere they twain slept fast at the uttermost end of the world

records.summary: Ralph and Ursula reach the end of the ness above the Ocean Sea.

records.label: Drinking of the Well

refs.q: To the Earth, and the World of Manfolk!

records.summary: Ralph and Ursula drink of the Well at the World's End and fall asleep.

records.label: After the draught

refs.q: it seemed to them that they had come into the very Garden of God

records.summary: They find their scars healed, bathe in a salt pool, and spend the evening in the tame meadows at the world's end.

records.label: Return through the Great Mountains

refs.q: their journey through the dreary pass was as light as it might be to any men

records.summary: The lovers return west with the Innocent Folk's help and cross the mountains.

records.label: Reunion with the Sage
places: (unnamed) Sage's bower by the blackthorn copse

refs.q: he deemed that it could be none other than the Sage of Swevenham

records.summary: The Sage, waiting since spring, meets the returning lovers at the Gate.

records.label: Fall of Gandolf

refs.q: I am verily Lord of Utterbol, and that by conquest

records.summary: The Lord of Utterbol (Gandolf) is slain and a new lord with the Bull arms takes Utterbol.

records.label: Winter with the Sage
places: (unnamed) house of the Sage of Swevenham

refs.q: So they dwelt there happily enough

records.summary: Ralph and Ursula winter at the hermitage and learn more from the Sage.

records.label: Meeting Bull, Lord of Utterbol

refs.q: though the feathers be fine 'tis the same bird

records.summary: At Vale Turris Ralph finds his former thrall Bull Shockhead now Lord of Utterbol.

records.label: Feast in the Red Pavilion

refs.q: Therewith he drank of the cup, and all men shouted

records.summary: At a feast Bull, Otter and Ralph swear oaths on the golden bull cup.

records.label: The lion in Goldburg market

refs.q: Eat in peace and safety, am I not here?

records.summary: Bull tames an escaped lion in Goldburg market and buys it.

records.label: Slaying of Gandolf

refs.q: thus endeth the worst man in the world

records.summary: Bull kills Gandolf in his chamber and is made Lord of Utterbol by Otter and the men-at-arms.

records.label: Drowning of the nephew
participants: (unnamed) nephew of the Lord of Utterbol

refs.q: two days before the slaying of his uncle, I met him in a wood

records.summary: Redhead drowns the Lord's nephew in the Ram's Bane two days before the Lord's death.

records.label: Departure from Vale Turris

refs.q: Bull and Otter kissed the wayfarers, and bade them farewell

records.summary: Bull and Otter escort the travellers till noon, then part.

records.label: Battle with the Black Riders
places: (unnamed) waste between Vale Turris and Goldburg

refs.q: in five minutes' time the Black Riders were fleeing all over the field

records.summary: On the fifth day the Utterbol escort routs the Black Riders; Ursula is struck but unhurt.

records.label: The vanished Queen of Goldburg
places: (unnamed) great wood down the Goldburg river

refs.q: she leapt out and let the thicket cover her

records.summary: A little over a year ago the Queen fled Goldburg by night down the river and vanished into a great wood.

records.label: Ralph before the King of Cheaping Knowe

refs.q: I crave of thee to give me life and limb and freedom for the poor folk whom I saw led down the hall

records.summary: Ralph awes the King by declaring he drank of the Well and wins freedom for condemned prisoners.

records.label: Death of the King of Cheaping Knowe

refs.q: in a few minutes there were no men of the foe together save those that were fleeing down the road to Cheaping Knowe

records.summary: Ambushing Ralph, the King of Cheaping Knowe is shot by the Folk of the Fells, who rout his men.

records.label: Three days with the Folk of the Fells
places: (unnamed) town of the Folk of the Fells

refs.q: the wild men wondered at his prowess

records.summary: The Folk of the Fells feast and hunt with Ralph and escort him to the plain.

records.label: Approach to Whitwall

refs.q: By my sword I swear it

records.summary: Nearing Whitwall, Ursula fears scorn and Ralph swears to stand by her against his kin.

records.label: Return to Whitwall

refs.q: he thrust the board from him, and arose and went to his harness

records.summary: Ralph meets Richard again, learns Walter the Black is dead, and leaves for Upmeads by night.

records.label: Ride from Whitwall

refs.q: It is well that we are here

records.summary: The four ride from Whitwall by the wildwood shortcut to avoid pursuit.

records.label: Death of the Captain of the Dry Tree

refs.q: Thus hath thy wish been accomplished

records.summary: The wild man attacks Ursula at the cave, is cut down, and dying is revealed as the Dry Tree's captain; he is buried beside the Lady.

records.label: Ralph becomes lord of Abundance

refs.q: Lament, ye people! for the Lady of Abundance is dead

records.summary: Ralph tells the folk of Abundance the Lady is dead and accepts their lordship.

records.label: Fall of the Burg of the Four Friths

refs.q: there befell that marvel which sometimes befalleth even to very valiant men

records.summary: The Dry Tree and the Wheat-wearers rout the Burg's hosts, take the Burg, and expel its people.

records.label: Return to the Burg

refs.q: So they entered the Flower de Luce, and had good welcome there

records.summary: Ralph's party enters the transformed Burg and lodges at the Flower de Luce.

records.label: Mote at the Scaur

refs.q: I swear that whensoever the Captain of the Dry Tree calleth on me

records.summary: In the Castle of the Scaur Ralph and the Dry Tree swear mutual oaths; the Scaur is offered to him.

records.label: Death of the old Queen of the Dry Tree
participants: (unnamed) old Queen of the Dry Tree

refs.q: we fell on the she-bear, as thou callest her, and her company of men and women

records.summary: After news of the Lady's death the Dry Tree fell on the old Queen; Roger slew her in the hall.

records.label: Turned away from Higham
participants: (unnamed) knight of Higham at the barrier

refs.q: Get thee behind us, Hugh, if thou wilt come with us, lad

records.summary: Higham refuses Ralph's Dry Tree band; Hugh escapes to join Ralph.

records.label: Battle of the Wry Bridge
participants: Abbot of St. Mary's of Higham

refs.q: there was Holy Church overthrown

records.summary: The Abbot of Higham's host is overthrown by the Westland Barons and the Abbot is taken to the Red Mount.
records.time_text: about a year and a half before

records.label: Ravaging of Higham-land

refs.q: the Westlanders broke their teeth over it

records.summary: The Westlanders fail to take Higham but take or burn most of the Abbot's castles.

records.label: Night at Garton

refs.q: meanwhile we will live and die together

records.summary: The thorp welcomes Ralph's company and young carles volunteer.

records.label: Martha's spaedom

refs.q: the Burg-devils will have come from the Wood Debateable to find graves by the fair river

records.summary: Martha foresees Ralph at Mileham, Milton or Garton, the mote at Bear Castle, friends at Wulstead, and the Burgers dying by the river of Upmeads.

records.label: Helper from afar

refs.q: a stripling and a great man; a runaway, and the conqueror of many

records.summary: The shepherds' tale of a helper from afar whose home is near.

records.label: Giles brings the message

refs.q: I shall gather my men, and ride the shortest way, which thou shalt show me, to Bear Castle

records.summary: Giles finds Ralph at Garton after midnight; Ralph plans Bear Castle, Wulstead, Upmeads.

records.label: Skirmish below the green ridge
places: (unnamed) dale below a low green ridge

refs.q: there was scarce time for a word ere the full half of them had passed by the sword of the Dry Tree

records.summary: Ralph surprises a Burger band, learns of the march on Upmeads, and takes twenty prisoners.

records.label: Muster at Bear Castle

refs.q: there were but some two hundreds, who looked but few indeed in the great square place

records.summary: Shepherds stream to Bear Castle; the four fires are lit.

records.label: Folkmote of the Shepherds

refs.q: all the Folk cried, "Hail our brother!"

records.summary: Ralph is made Captain and brother of the Shepherds; the host musters at 554.

records.label: Arrival at Wulstead

refs.q: they all streamed into the street

records.summary: Clement welcomes Ralph and Ursula; the host enters Wulstead behind Ursula bearing the guisarme.

records.label: Ralph meets his parents
places: House of Black Canons of Wulstead

refs.q: here is a daughter and a darling that I have brought back to thee, for this is my wedded wife

records.summary: Ralph and Ursula meet King Peter and the Dame in the canons' church at Wulstead.

records.label: Night council at Wulstead

refs.q: O my lord, my lord, thou art come again to us!

records.summary: Ralph hears that the Burgers are in Upmeads, orders the muster, and is reunited with Katherine.

records.label: Katherine and the Wise Woman of Sarras

refs.q: Thou shalt take this pair of beads, and do with them as I bid thee

records.summary: In Sarras the Holy the Wise Woman teaches Katherine and gives her the beads destined for Ralph.

records.label: Muster at Wulstead

refs.q: blowing men to the gathering

records.summary: At dawn the four trumpets call the host to the market-place.

records.label: Battle of Upmeads

refs.q: great and grim was the murder

records.summary: Ralph's host breaks the Burgers on the hill above Upmeads; Nicholas holds the Bridge.
records.time_text: morning, done an hour before noon

records.label: Return of King Peter to Upmeads

refs.q: So Ralph led his father and his mother to the gate of the garth of High House

records.summary: Ralph brings his parents home to the High House.

records.label: Crowning feast at the High House

refs.q: they cried hail to the King of Upmeads

records.summary: Ralph is set on the throne and proclaimed King of Upmeads, Ursula Queen.

records.label: Peter's foretelling

refs.q: he shall be lord and servant of other lands than Upmeads

records.summary: Peter foresees Ralph drawing towns, kindreds and lords into peace and might.

records.label: Ralph's reign

refs.q: he ruled over his lands in right and might

records.summary: Ralph rules Upmeads, holds the Scaur, leads the Burg, the Dry Tree and the Shepherds, and pacifies Higham and both woods.

records.label: Bull's visit

refs.q: did him right manly service in battle

records.summary: About two years later the Lord Bull of Utterbol, with Otter and Redhead, rides to battle with Ralph and stays two months.
records.time_text: about two years after the homecoming

records.label: Death of Ralph and Ursula

refs.q: On one day they two died and were laid together in one tomb in the choir of St. Laurence of Upmeads

records.summary: They die on one day and are laid in one tomb in St. Laurence's choir.
